description: Retire the CDS ERA5-Land soil lane for its keyless Open-Meteo equivalent, close the et0-model trap that would silently persist an all-NULL signal, and add four new upstream datasets -- fire-weather VPD, GloFAS river discharge, CAMS air quality, and ensemble forecast uncertainty -- through the durable-backfill and Railway-cron standards already established

pivot_reconciliation_20260822.verdict: still valid, needs rescoping. Status changed from the registry's stale 'planned' to 'blocked': the track's OWN plan.md already carries a detailed, honest 2026-08-06 post-implementation review recording specific, still-open blockers -- this is not new information, it was simply never propagated to tracks.md.
pivot_reconciliation_20260822.evidence_confirmed_in_tree_20260822: execution/historical_glofas.py, execution/historical_cams.py, ingest/open_meteo_air_quality.py, ingest/open_meteo_ensemble.py, execution/ensemble_forecast.py, execution/historical_writer/{glofas,cams}.py, plans/open-meteo-era5-land-pnw-vpd-*.json all exist -- matches the plan's own 'built' claims for phases 1-4. Introduced in commit c01ed48 (2026-08-06, message: 'GloFAS, CAMS and Ensemble lanes on shared scaffolding; VPD whitelisted; soil-field day rule hardened'). No infra/cron-flood-discharge/, infra/cron-air-quality/, or infra/cron-ensemble-forecast/ directories exist (only cron-ingest, cron-mtbs, cron-soilgrids do) -- confirms the plan's own finding (e) that the staged cron configs were removed as non-functional and never re-added. No RUNBOOK.md mention of GloFAS/CAMS/VPD/ensemble exists after 2026-08-07, so no evidence of further progress since the track's own review.
pivot_reconciliation_20260822.named_blockers_still_open: Per the track's own plan.md follow-up section: (a) historical_writer.py persist verbs for GloFAS/CAMS never written -- both lanes fetch/validate/cache but cannot land a warehouse row; (b) the forecast_method/model_kind CHECK-constraint widening migration for the Ensemble lane's provenance was never authored; (c) the et0 model-guard structural test was never added -- the trap Phase 0 exists to close is still closeable only by convention; (d) no serving-side reads, geo views, or layer-registry entries exist for GloFAS/CAMS -- confirmed no 'glofas' or 'cams' reference in layer-registry.ts or useViewportProxiedLayers.ts.
pivot_reconciliation_20260822.pivot_interaction: The pivot changes what 'persistence' means for blocker (a): instead of authoring historical_writer.py Postgres persist verbs, the natural post-pivot fix is a Parquet-lane writer, which may be strictly less work. But none of GloFAS (river discharge) or CAMS (air quality) appear in §0.24.2's 11 named lanes (weather-observations, sensors, water-gauges, vegetation, fire-detections, fire-perimeters, burn-severity, interventions, soil-survey, watersheds, evacuation-zones). VPD (Phase 1) most likely folds into weather-observations. GloFAS is arguably adjacent to water-gauges (USGS streamflow) but is a different upstream (a global river-discharge model, not gauge readings) and was flagged in the track's own Phase 2 as possibly needing its own entity concept rather than the existing spatial-cell lattice. CAMS has no obvious lane at all. This is an open scoping question for the owner, not something this pass resolved.
pivot_reconciliation_20260822.recommendation: Do not resume Phases 2-4 as Postgres-persistence work. Before resuming: (1) owner decides whether GloFAS/CAMS get their own lanes, fold into an existing one, or wait past wave 2; (2) blocker (c), the et0 structural guard, is small and lane-independent and could land any time; (3) blocker (b), the CHECK-constraint migration, should be re-evaluated once S20's serving path is defined, since 'ml'/'sql_linear' as forecast_method may not even be the right vocabulary post-pivot.

dependency_mode: Python only inside services/agri-data-service/src/agri_data_service (new OPEN_METEO_ARCHIVE_SIGNAL_SPECIFICATIONS entries, new ingest/ and execution/historical_* modules). No Alembic revision for any phase: agri.data_source.key is a free-text unique column registered by DML at ingest/backfill time, not DDL, and the ensemble phase's open schema question is answered inside that same no-DDL ceiling or explicitly deferred. New infra/cron-flood-discharge/, infra/cron-air-quality/, infra/cron-ensemble-forecast/ directories follow the existing infra/cron-*/railway.json pattern (railway.json only, reusing infra/cron-ingest/Dockerfile's shared image). Two things happen outside this repository and outside any agent's authority: unregistering the PlantGeo-ERA5-PNW-backfill Windows scheduled task, and the Railway dashboard Root Directory + config-as-code path pair for each new cron service, which must change together the way plantgeo-ingest-cron's did. Every dataset addition is a new plan file, a new release_set.logical_key, and a new manifest_checksum -- never an edit to an existing plan.
activation_gate: Phase 0 lands first: it edits the same OPEN_METEO_ARCHIVE_SIGNAL_SPECIFICATIONS block in historical_open_meteo.py that Phase 1's vapour_pressure_deficit_max entry lands in, and its CDS retirement removes the scheduled task and plan files that a Phase-1-only reading of the repo would otherwise still show as live. Phase 1 is verified (3.32 kPa, live) and ready to ship the moment Phase 0 merges -- it needs no probe. Phases 2 through 4 each open with a live-endpoint probe confirming field names and response shape, the same discipline that produced the 3.32 kPa figure, before any checksummed plan is authored -- an unverified variable name in a plan costs a full re-fetch to correct, not an edit. Phase 4 additionally carries an open schema question (whether an ensemble member is a quantile reduction into the existing forecast_receipt/forecast_value quantile columns, or a raw per-member row needing new storage) that the owner must answer before backfill authoring, though the probe and the cron wiring do not wait on it. Phases 1 through 4 touch disjoint files after Phase 0 and may ship in any order or in parallel.
